title: A Fire on the Opposite Shore
text: Once the wave had ended, the skies near the towns and villages were blue again, though in the distance the clouds still seemed to churn and swirl. As I thought about it, there was no doubt that the damage had been far more terrible than the wave we had fought in. Come to think of it, food shortages were also starting to surface as a problem.

A bitterly cold wind blew with a mournful whoosh. It seemed Éclair’s parent was heading toward the castle, bringing along Éclair and a formidable escort. They would form a procession and travel by carriage, making straight for the castle. Between the personnel left to guard the territory and the escort capable of fighting alongside Éclair’s parent, things seemed like they would manage somehow. Older Sister, meanwhile, showed no sign of being able to travel far, since she needed to protect the village. Well… given that the Three Heroes Church thugs had been driven off, it wasn’t likely they’d launch an immediate counteroffensive.

Still, I had to admit—this was turning into an awfully troublesome situation. …Perhaps I ought to just burn down the Three Heroes Church’s cathedral? Various thoughts swirled through my head. Those fools had used the wave as an excuse, calling it divine judgment to justify their aggression. If that’s the case, then I thought it only fitting to deliver judgment upon them in turn, quite literally. Surely that would calm them down a little, would it not?

The question was which to do first. And so, cloaked in invisibility and wearing my usapil disguise, I approached Older Sister, who was making her way back toward the village, waiting until I confirmed there were few people around before calling out to her.
“Mind if I ask you something real quick?”
“…Oh? What can I do for you?”

Older Sister turned to face me, her brow slightly furrowed, clearly past the point of doubting anything after the wave. Naturally, I pointed in the direction Éclair’s parent’s group had gone before asking my question.
“I’m a bit concerned about Éclair’s parent, the lord of this territory here. Would it be better for me to keep watch over the village or the town instead?”
“Hmm… I’d like you to leave the village to me, but the town should be able to manage its own defenses well enough, and with the lord away, I think it should be fine, don’t you think?”
Thought as much, didn’t I?
“Well then, I’ve got something else I wanted to run by you.”
“What is it you want to ask Older Sister?”
“This is getting tiresome, so would it be alright if I blew up the Three Heroes Church’s headquarters cathedral in the castle town with magic?”

I intended to recreate what I’d done in that other loop—the one where I’d successfully talked some sense into Ren and Itsuki, exposed the Crimson Swine’s crimes, and rescued Father from his false charges. If I burned the cathedral down with Liberation Firestorm, surely that would leave them no time for outrageous schemes like assassinating Éclair’s parent, would it not? It was, quite literally, the perfect time to call it the wave’s judgment.
“Oh my… that’s quite the dangerous proposal. Older Sister’s being asked some troublesome things today.”
Older Sister furrowed her brow.
“Sadeena-neesan, who are you talking to?”
Oh? Big Sister had noticed Older Sister in the middle of our conversation and called out to her. Older Sister’s expression went rigid. I made no move, of course.
“’Tis I, peep!”
I gazed at Big Sister with my eyes shining as brightly as I could manage, going full kyururin.
“Who’s that?”
“The name’s Usaunny, peep! Just a traveler, peep!”
“Oh, is that so?”
“Y-Yes…”
Older Sister nodded while keeping her attention on Big Sister.
“This here Older Sister and I go way back, peep. Just checking if she was alright with all this commotion going on, peep.”
A bit of improvised nonsense to smooth things over, peep.
“That’s right, so Raphtalia-chan, it’s still dangerous around here, so hurry on home now.”
“But…”

“Seems like there are some troublemakers lurking around these parts, so we’d best get back quick, Older Sister thinks. And, Usaunny-chan, Older Sister doesn’t think you should go causing too much of a ruckus, you hear?”

With that, Older Sister hastily scooped Big Sister up and hurried off. Hmm… so I’m not meant to blow up the cathedral, then? Considering how full of themselves those fanatics must be, riding high on their little victory, I rather thought giving them a good smack would be the right call… What would Father do in this case, I wondered? If I pictured the Father from the loop where he couldn’t be saved from his false accusations, he’d probably agree, saying something like, “Well, they twisted the wave to suit their own agenda, so why not give it right back to them?”

Then again, the kinder Father might also say, “Hmm… if they decide it wasn’t the Heroes who did it, they might just use it as another excuse, claiming the Demi-Humans and Beastmen retaliated instead.”

Still, I couldn’t help recalling what happened when I blasted that cathedral back when we went to Faubrey. All that amounted to was a lesson that the head simply grows back. But this time was different—the wave was being used as a pretext for the nobles to invade Éclair’s territory. So if I framed this too as a consequence of the wave, I figured it could plausibly be tied together now.

Alright! To put the Three Heroes Church in its place, a bit more smacking down was clearly in order! With that decided, I immediately opened a portal to Melromarc’s castle town to check things out. The people there were going about their daily lives, though their faces were etched with unease.
“Hey, did you hear? Some crazy storm tore through and the sea went completely wild, or so they say.”
“Ah… something about the church claiming it was the arrival of the legendary ‘end-times wave’ foretold in prophecy. Said it was certain since the Dragon Hourglass had run out of sand.”
“Huh, but that’s the region where the Demi-Humans live, right?”
“Yeah, yeah, and apparently the damage was pretty severe.”
“Serves ’em right, I say.”
Rumors passed from mouth to mouth among the crowd, each voice adding its own commentary. But to them, it was all just a fire on the opposite shore—someone else’s problem entirely.
“I heard Lord Seaetto, who was handling official duties alongside the Wise Sage King while the Queen’s away, got caught up in the disaster.”
“Would be nice if he just up and died, honestly—world’d be better off.”
“Someone ought to purify those filthy beasts, I say.”
Just as I’d expected, such extremist sentiments had taken deep root among certain factions within Melromarc.

Just then—ah, right, I remembered now—a soldier who hailed from Lute Village, near Melromarc’s castle town, walked past with his brow furrowed and fists clenched. I recalled, albeit hazily, that some Demi-Humans served among the soldiers. This one must have been a colleague of theirs. Not an extremist, so I had no memory of ever having taken him down. It seemed he was guarding the country despite clearly feeling discomfort at the words of his fellow Melromarc citizens. An unusual fellow to cross paths with, but that wasn’t my concern at the moment. Now then… let me scout ahead to the castle and check what’s happening inside. What’s Trash up to, I wonder? Heading toward the throne room, I found Trash seated upon his throne, wearing a deeply troubled expression.
“The wave, hm… Malty… please come home soon.”
Worrying over the Crimson Swine of all things. Foolishness, plain and simple.
“What is the situation with Seaetto and the others?”
“Sir! Despite our kingdom’s knights and soldiers rushing to aid in the rescue efforts, we received word that our hands were rebuffed, resulting in casualties!”
“Hmm…”
Trash’s expression darkened further. I’d expected him to be pleased, but his reaction was something else entirely.
“…What of Seaetto’s safety?”
“His survival has been confirmed. It is suspected he may be harboring a grudge over the wave’s damage and could be plotting to march on the castle.”
“…It seems unlikely to me that the one entrusted with domestic affairs by my wife during her absence would resort to such reckless action…”

Even Trash tilted his head in confusion at his aide’s suggestion. The Three Heroes Church lot were pushing forward with unreasonable schemes even under these circumstances. Since it made no logical sense, even Trash wasn’t buying it.
“Wise Sage King! Please, let us march forth to stop Seaetto’s rampage! Now is the time to finally end his life!”
Trash’s expression made it clear he thought this was simply wrong.
“And if I leave the castle undefended, who exactly is meant to guard it?”
